text:
driftbot: DRIFT ALERT — env parity check failed for cluster prod-us-west1

driftbot: Resource: nodepool/gpu-us-west1
driftbot: Field diff: spec.autoscaling.minReplicas: staging=2 -> prod=4; spec.taints: staging=[gpu:NoSchedule] -> prod=[gpu:NoSchedule, spot:PreferNoSchedule]
driftbot: Triggered by: nightly-env-diff (run 2021f-ops-483) — https://internal.ops/diffs/1918002345

sam: Is this new? CI shows a reconcile ran around 00:12 UTC.

leah: Yep, I saw the alert. It looks like terraform apply from infra-ci created a new auto-scale policy yesterday. Not sure why gitops didn't reconcile down.

mike: Quick peek at the operator logs: `k8s-reconcile-controller` keeps getting `403 Forbidden` when trying to patch nodepool object:
```
E0321 00:13:10 reconcile.go:142] patch failed: patching nodepool gpu-us-west1: API error: status=403, body="iam: permission denied: resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy"
```

anya: That 403 smells like a service account permission gap. infra-ci-bot probably lost the `compute.nodePools.update` role on the project after the last IAM cleanup.

infra-ci-bot: recent run 2021f-ops-483: applied module.gke.nodepools["gpu-us-west1"] -> updated autoscaling.minReplicas=4 (manual override flag set: true)

sam: So two things: prod is drifted because an override got applied directly, and the controller/agent can't revert because it lacks permissions. We should not have manual overrides without a corresponding IAM grant.

leah: Also note the taint diff includes `spot:PreferNoSchedule` in prod. That was introduced by a cost experiment last week (spot-fallback-branch). If nodepool now has mixed taints, scheduling and eviction behavior will differ. Could affect latency for inference pods.

mike: Action plan: I'll open a short-lived privileged job to patch the nodepool back to minReplicas=2 and remove the spot taint so staging parity restored. Then we can re-run the reconcile. If privilege patch fails, escalate to cloud support.

anya: Add a guard: infra-ci should add a preflight policy check that prevents manual override without `roles/container.admin` scoped to the nodepool service account. Also add an alert when overrides are set outside GitOps.

sam: I'll create the ticket and assign: INFRA-844. Steps in ticket: 1) run manual patch (mike) 2) verify pod placement & autoscaler metrics for 30m (leah) 3) add IAM fix & preflight (anya + sam) 4) post-mortem of who flipped the override (audit)

mike: Starting manual patch now: `gcloud container node-pools update gpu-us-west1 --cluster=redwood-prod --region=us-west1 --min-nodes=2 --node-taints="gpu:NoSchedule"`

leah: Watching logs. If pods start thrashing we may need to cordon/evict gracefully. Will post metrics in INFRA-844 thread. :eyes:

sam: Also thought: our drift-detector should include quota checks. There were only 6 GPUs left in us-west1 yesterday; someone launched a training job and that bumped allocations. If autoscaler tried to scale down and then another request scaled up, the manual override might have been a last-minute workaround. We should add a quick 'quota-sanity' rule in the reconcile pipeline.

mike: Noted. I'll include quota-checks in the PR for the operator.

infra-ci-bot: CI preflight queued for INFRA-PR-511: adds opa policy `deny_manual_override_without_iam` and a new quota-sanity check for gpu quotas.

sam: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open while we validate — please ping me directly if you need escalation. :thumbsup:
